title: Validation of a canonical field
statement: Let $x,w$ be finite bit strings, let $f$ be one of the three field indices, let $v$ be an assignment of natural numbers to the 13 registers, and let $b$ be a Boolean answer. Assume every register is at most $4(|x|+1)$. Suppose that one program step from the field-test state goes to the next validation state when $w$ is empty, and otherwise goes to the field-clear state. If $w$ is nonempty, suppose the bit of $x$ at the position obtained from the designated source register by subtracting $1$ when $f$ is the third field and $2$ otherwise (with natural-number subtraction truncated at zero) agrees with the last bit of $w$, taking out-of-range bits to be false. Assume also that a noncanonical $w$ forces $b$ to be false, and that for canonical $w$, every bounded register assignment agreeing with $v$ on all registers other than register $0$ yields a halting run from the next validation state with answer $b$. Then the run from the field-test state halts with answer $b$, maintaining the program’s safety conditions before halting.
